clauses.requirement: For the position of the lamp as regards width (UN R48 para 5.8, where maximum/minimum height is measured on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis), the position shall be determined from the edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis furthest from the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle when referred to overall width, and from the inner edges of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis when referred to the distance between lamps; where the position as regards width clearly meets the requirements of the Regulation, the exact edges of any surface need not be determined.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics of the rear lamp functions (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface) shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.

Direction-indicator lamps, the vehicle-hazard warning signal, amber side-marker lamps complying with paragraph 6.18.7 of UN R48, and the emergency stop signal shall be flashing lamps; if the rear lamp incorporates a direction-indicator function (not listed for this product) it shall be a flashing lamp, while rear position, stop and reversing functions remain non-varied in operation per para 5.9.

The photometric characteristics of any lamp (including rear position, stop and reversing functions) may vary only (a) in relation to the ambient light, (b) as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, or (c) when the lamp is being used to provide another lighting function, provided that any variation complies with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.

If a direction indicator lamp of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a or 2b is used (not listed for this product), its photometric characteristics may be varied during a flash by sequential activation of light sources as specified in paragraph 5.6 of UN Regulation No. 6 or paragraph 5.6.11 of UN Regulation No. [LSD]; this provision shall not apply when direction indicator lamps of categories 2a and 2b are operated as emergency stop signal according to paragraph 6.23.1 of UN R48.

If an answer-back signal is provided using the lamp(s), the signal may flash and/or vary in luminous intensity and/or vary in apparent surface, and the lamp(s) used for the answer-back signal shall operate according to the conditions specified in the general specifications and/or in dedicated paragraph 6.27 of UN R48.
If the reversing lamp provides a reversing projection, the projection may vary according to the steering wheel angle and/or the speed of the vehicle and/or the proximity to an obstacle.

The rear lamp shall comply with the provisions of UN R48 para 5.10 regarding light which could give rise to confusion (heading of the provisions listed under that paragraph); no light emitted by the lamp shall give rise to confusion.
